rubric field names required/allowed_question_topics and required/allowed_revision_facts; single global concept_definitions map; coarse reusable revision tokens

method.categorical: route, responsibility, tone and overall are decided by majority of the three labeler votes. A two-of-three majority is adopted on the evidence and the rubric; three distinct values would make the turn gold_uncertain.
method.overall: the adjudicated overall status is re-derived from the adjudicated responsibility and tone with the rubric priority Red > Gray > Yellow > Green, and checked against the majority overall vote.
method.concept_normalisation: the three label sets use different concept vocabularies. Every labeler token is mapped to a canonical concept, taking ontology ids where they exist and coarse local ids otherwise; fine-grained case-specific tokens roll up into the coarse canonical concept they instantiate, and a coarse token whose own definition and rationale instantiate it more narrowly is mapped through a recorded context override.
method.required_concepts: a canonical concept is required in gold when at least two labelers required a token that normalises to it. A concept required by one labeler only is demoted to the allowed set rather than dropped.
method.allowed_concepts: the allowed set is the union of every canonical concept any labeler required or allowed, so that a semantically acceptable output concept is not scored as unnecessary or unsupported. no-revision is excluded from the allowed set when the adjudicated overall status is not Green.
method.no_revision_entailment: a labeler that required no-revision is counted as requiring no rewrite content; the preserve-style concepts such a stance trivially entails are counted towards the allowed set only, never towards required votes.
method.critical_invariants: each invariant token is adopted when at least two labelers list it for that turn.
method.uncertainty: a turn is marked gold_uncertain when a categorical field carries three distinct labeler values, or when a substantive critical-invariant disagreement cannot be resolved by majority.
context_override_notes: kimi disclose-material-context on V3-015 turns 2 and 3 is instantiated in that labeler's own rationale as disclosing that Elsa already told Aleksi the blanks would be accepted, so it normalises to disclose-prior-commitment rather than to the generic omitted-context concept.

approval-authority.definition: Ask who has authority to approve or decide.

blocker-status.definition: Ask whether a blocker exists and what it is.

commitment-scope.definition: Ask which work, period, or boundary the sender can commit to.

confirm-obscured-image-value.definition: Ask the sender to restate a value or token that exists only inside a supplied image and is occluded, illegible, or glyph-ambiguous.

confirmed-deadline.definition: Ask for the current confirmed completion or delivery date.

confirmed-owner.definition: Ask who currently owns the work or decision.

current-root-cause.definition: Ask what caused the current incident or failure.

disclose-material-context.definition: Add material case facts the draft omits that the recipient needs in order to understand or decide.

disclose-prior-commitment.definition: State plainly that the sender has already committed something or already told a third party something material.

exact-measurement.definition: Ask for the exact numeric measurement the recipient or the safety context requires when only a coarse description of the reading is in hand.

no-revision.definition: No revision is needed for a Green message.

omit-unsupported-figure.definition: Leave out a figure the case data does not support.

operational-impact.definition: Ask for the concrete execution or customer impact.

placeholder-unknown-value.definition: Represent a required unknown value with a descriptive placeholder.

preserve-confirmed-deadline.definition: Keep the confirmed date or deadline unchanged.

preserve-image-text.definition: Preserve image text exactly as rendered, including glyph-ambiguous tokens, and mark unreadable image text as unknown rather than normalising or guessing it.

preserve-intended-recipient.definition: Keep the user-identified recipient or audience.

preserve-material-facts.definition: Keep the material facts the case supports, including figures, references, owners, dates, prior actions and constraints, and state confirmed observations plainly rather than hedging them.

qualify-unconfirmed-cause.definition: State that a cause or attribution remains unconfirmed.

qualify-unconfirmed-impact.definition: Present an expected operational effect as expected or unconfirmed rather than certain.

reclaim-owned-task.definition: State that the sender will complete work that sits in their own scope instead of assigning it elsewhere.

remove-client-contact-claim.definition: Remove a claim that the client or external party has already been told, and keep that party off a thread they are not on.

remove-defensive-framing.definition: Neutralise self-blame, apology stacking, blame-shifting and other defensive framing that obscures the message.

remove-false-reassurance.definition: Remove or condition reassurance the case data does not support, such as saying a matter is fine, settled, or nothing to worry about.

remove-hostile-language.definition: Remove insult, ridicule and hostile framing while keeping the supported factual core, and hold the register the channel requires.

remove-unsafe-commitment.definition: Remove or condition a commitment that lacks authority or confirmed scope.

remove-unsupported-accusation.definition: Remove or neutralize an unsupported blame or intent claim.

respect-channel-constraint.definition: Hold the required channel, length, line count, register or plain-language constraint.

route-to-authority.definition: Leave the decision, approval or action with the person or function that owns it, and ask that owner to decide or ratify instead of announcing or pre-empting the decision.

state-clear-ask.definition: Include the concrete ask, decision point or recommendation the recipient's authority calls for.

withhold-unsupported-conclusion.definition: Do not state a conclusion before it is stood up in the supporting work.

coverage.reporting_rule: coverage is reported as adjudicated. No label was adjusted to reach any v3 coverage target, and no v3 coverage gate, methodology, scorer or spec file was read.
honest_coverage_notes: Every turn in this case set is a rated Normal mode turn, so the Intake, Scope, Message-template and Limited-background routes carry no gold coverage here and null ratings never occur.
Gray appears on exactly one turn, V3-017 turn 1, and only on the responsibility axis.
Required question concepts appear on two turns only, because on most turns no question topic could change the route, rating or safe revision and the labelers agreed on that.

V3-006 turn 1 carries an empty required revision set: the three labelers proposed non-overlapping revision concepts, so nothing reached a two-of-three majority. The set was left empty rather than widened to satisfy a coverage expectation.
no-image-token-guess is adjudicated onto the two image-only turns only, matching the two labelers that scope it to image cases.

limitations: Labeler rationale prose is not copied into this record; every categorical vote, raw concept list and invariant list is preserved verbatim, and the rationales stay in the three labeler files.
Semantic normalisation of three different concept vocabularies is adjudicator judgement. The full token map and every context override are recorded so each roll-up can be audited and reversed.

Because two of the three label sets use coarse reusable concepts and one uses fine-grained case-specific concepts, majority counting happens at the coarse level; fine distinctions from the grok set survive in this record and in the per-turn labeler_token_aliases of the gold file.

One labeler omitted no-prompt-override on all 24 turns and no-unsafe-commitment on some turns, so critical_invariant_disagreement is true on every turn under the literal definition used here; the distinction between that systematic convention difference and case-specific contested tokens is recorded per turn and counted separately in the summary.
Model identity of this adjudicator is unverified; only the declared model family is recorded.
